label: H2 (refined after the bank screen): the closing object/amount (or final period) of a hypothetical projection claim that a deliberate action or intervention WOULD/COULD change a measurable quantity -- money accumulated or saved, a bill or cost reduced, efficiency/yield/return raised, risk lowered -- typically with a possessor or a number on the target ('would have close to N3,000', 'would reduce your electricity bill', 'could increase their efficiency'). Weaker for will/may/present-tense action->result statements; near-silent for natural-event conditionals, abstract economic/physical laws, descriptive mentions of the same quantities, and code returns (the corpus code/long-context peaks did not reproduce in isolation, so H2 only claims the short-sentence prose behaviour).
